messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing cross-project responses coming from the token cache path after yesterday's RBAC refactor. Repro'd on staging.
aj: Which endpoints are affected? can you paste a minimal log?
maria: Example from staging logs:
```
2026-02-10T14:02:13Z service=runtime user=svc-agent project_id=proj-B org_id=org-123 cache_key=org-123:aliasX token_id=tok-7f3 response_project=proj-A
```
Looks like requests for proj-B are returning cached responses for proj-A when namespace aliasing is enabled.
devon: That's the namespace aliaser + cache-key salt logic we changed in PR #3421, right?
maria: Yup. Quick diff shows we now derive cache salt from org_id + alias only — we dropped project_id. That produces collisions for multiple projects in the same org.
aj: Is this happening only with JWTs or also with KMS-wrapped tokens?
maria: Observed both, but KMS-wrapped tokens are worse: the decrypt path uses the unwrap service principal which currently doesn't enforce project-scoped ACLs, so a stale cached plaintext can be returned across projects.
chen: Is this cross-org or intra-org? severity estimate?
maria: Intra-org only (same org, different projects). Potentially leaks project-scoped templates/secrets. Treat as P2 for now.
devon: Mitigation plan: disable namespace aliasing in the cache layer and purge affected cache entries. I can push a hotfix feature-flag flip.
aj: Rolling back PR #3421 in the serving runtime might be faster in parallel.
devon: I'll flip the cache feature flag and run a purge for org-123. ETA ~15m.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045. Pager duty and incident channel notified.
devon: flip done. Purge command running:
```
# find keys for org-123 and delete
redis-cli --scan | grep "org:123:" | xargs -r redis-cli del
```
maria: Can confirm after purge cache_key now includes project id again. Re-running repro: no cross-project responses seen.
aj: Good. Postmortem items: add unit tests for cache key salt, integration test for KMS decrypt path that asserts project_id enforcement.
chen: I'll own the postmortem. Can we add an eval/regression in Redwood Optimize to detect cross-project output leakage?
maria: Yes — add regression alerts that run prompt sets with project-specific markers and fail if outputs contain other project ids. Also add KMS audit-log linkage to token IDs.
devon: Follow-ups I'm opening: 1) require explicit project_id param for aliasing, 2) add cache-key unit tests, 3) add ACL check in KMS decrypt path, 4) GA alert for cache collisions. I'll open PRs and link them.
aj: :thumbsup: Also run analytics across prod cache for collisions over the last 7 days — I'll kick off a query and post results here.
maria: If analytics finds suspicious collisions, rotate the service key used for KMS unwrap for the org and prepare customer notification if secret exposure is likely.
aj: Query scheduled, will update.
devon: Created infra issue: https://git.internal/rw/infra/issues/581 — linking PRs and notes there.
maria: Thanks. Please also update the SOC compliance log: note key-scope misalignment and mitigations taken.
chen: Will update SOC log and draft the postmortem timeline.
maria: Great work everyone. We'll follow up with SLA impact assessment and customer comms if needed. :wave:
